concepts.def: The Sun, eight planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
Planets orbit the Sun in ellipses.
Gravity provides the centripetal force for orbits.
Icy bodies on highly elliptical orbits.
Rocky bodies, mostly between Mars and Jupiter.
Bodies like Pluto that don't clear their orbit.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Solar Astronomy — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Solar Astronomy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Solar Astronomy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Length of the solar cycle (sunspot count)?
options: 1 year
11 years
22 years
50 years

mcqs.q: Charged particles streaming from the Sun are called?
options: Solar flares
Solar wind
Aurora
Cosmic rays

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: Telescopes distort star positions.
It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.
Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.
It is made of fire.

mcqs.q: What is the principle behind stellar parallax?
options: Stars actually move position throughout the year.
Telescopes distort star positions.
A nearby star appears to shift against background stars as Earth orbits the Sun.
Light gets tired and loses energy.

mcqs.q: What does cosmological redshift tell us?
options: Light gets tired and loses energy.
It is made of fire.
Galaxies are turning red as they age.
Galaxies are receding from us due to the expansion of space.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solar cycle”?
options: Cooler regions (~3,800 K) on the photosphere with strong magnetic fields (~0.3 T).
Sudden intense burst of X-ray and UV radiation from magnetic reconnection above sunspots.
~11-year cycle of sunspot number and magnetic activity; full magnetic cycle is 22 years.
Glows from atmospheric atoms excited by solar particles channelled along Earth's field lines.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solar flare”?
options: Huge eruption of plasma and magnetic field into space; can cause geomagnetic storms.
Sudden intense burst of X-ray and UV radiation from magnetic reconnection above sunspots.
~11-year cycle of sunspot number and magnetic activity; full magnetic cycle is 22 years.
Continuous stream of charged particles flowing from the Sun's corona at 400-800 km/s.
